intro_html: Chicken cacciatore is rustic Italian at its finest, all peppers, mushrooms, and tomato simmered until the flavors marry. This version tosses it with penne for a hearty pasta bowl at 67 grams of protein and about $4.35 a serving (at everyday cost). One batch makes 14 servings, so a Sunday in the slow cooker sets up more than a week of dinners.
cost_closing_html: About $4.35 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving carries 67 grams of protein and 570 calories, a genuinely high-protein pasta plate.
upsell_html: Big-batch Italian comfort that reheats like a dream. This one's a keeper. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: A jar of traditional pasta sauce beats making it from scratch on both time and cost, so grab the store-brand jar and doctor it with the veg.
Peppers and mushrooms are cheapest in season and on sale, so let the markdown bin pick your vegetables.
Cook the pasta separately and store it apart from the sauce, so it won't turn to mush over a week of reheating.
make_it: Add the chicken, pasta sauce, sliced mushrooms, chopped bell peppers, onion, olive oil, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken shreds and the vegetables are tender.
Shred the chicken into the sauce and stir everything together.
Boil the penne separately until just al dente and drain it.
Toss the pasta with the cacciatore sauce, or spoon the sauce over each portion of pasta.
